page.topic: EcoCare condition-based maintenance and remote monitoring service plans
page.industry: Cross-industry (electrical distribution, UPS, data centers, buildings)
target_prompts: Which condition-based maintenance and remote monitoring service plans exist for electrical distribution and UPS equipment?
fan_out: Which EcoCare plans/tiers exist per equipment type and how do they differ?
What service levels apply (coverage hours, response / time-to-site, visits per year)?
Which equipment ranges and models are eligible, including third-party gear?
How does remote monitoring work (connectivity, data flow, cybersecurity)?
What measured results have customers achieved, and on what basis?

criteria.rationale: 24/7 coverage and an escalation path (notify, remote troubleshoot, dispatch), but no numeric response/restore commitment or tier conditions (-> <= 2).
Equipment categories named and gateway connectivity prerequisite implied; no models/ranges or multi-vendor coverage.
Named references without results; credentials (Connected Services Hub, IEC 62443-4-1, CREST) present; c2 fail -> <= 2.
Plans named per equipment type only; no differences, contract/pricing model or availability.
Brand-centred promotional voice ('your answer to', 'unlock exclusive benefits', 'peace of mind'); no limits.
Four ordered step labels with roles of the Connected Services Hub, but steps are not explained in place and no start of engagement.
Three 'up to' outcomes attributed to EcoCare, one with a baseline (vs calendar-based plans), but footnotes 1-3 never resolve (level >= 4 needs c5).
Concrete included activities (24/7 monitoring, break-fix, CBM, success plan, training) with remote vs on-site split; no exclusions or add-on list.
Descriptive headings, feature lists and short paragraphs, but plan cards are cloned titles without text and the how-it-works explanations sit only in a hidden carousel (key facts hidden -> <= 2).
Body definition within ~70 words and title matches the prompt; H1 is a slogan; 'How EcoCare works' and other H2s do not open with answers; no summary.
Evaluation needs plan differences and SLAs, which are absent; only CTA is generic 'Contact Sales' (does not name the service); links to plans by equipment type.
What and when (shift from time-based maintenance) are clear; no audience named in the top block; outcome is a 'help maximize' promise.

disclaimer: Citation-readiness of content only; actual AI citation also depends on retrieval, off-site consensus and technical access.
